g.text: Angle Preservation Condition // Elementary Mappings // Möbius Engine // Cross-Ratio Invariance // Fixed Points
Isogonal property // Preservation of angle magnitude and orientation // Critical points
A mapping w = f(z) is conformal at point z₀ iff:
• Angle magnitude between any two intersecting curves is strictly preserved.
• Sense of rotation (clockwise / counterclockwise) is strictly preserved.
• Local linear scale magnification factor = |f'(z₀)| | Rotation angle = arg(f'(z₀))
A point z₀ where f'(z₀) = 0 is called a Critical Point.
• If f'(z₀) = ... = fⁿ⁻¹(z₀) = 0 and fⁿ(z₀) ≠ 0, angles are multiplied by factor n!
Example: w = z² ⇒ w' = 2z = 0 at z = 0. Angle at origin is DOUBLED!
Preserves magnitude of angles, but reverses sense of rotation (e.g. w = z̄).
u = x + a, v = y + b
Preserves size, shape, and orientation of all curves.
Maps circle through origin to straight line not through origin!
Horizontal strip 0 < y < π maps to upper half plane v > 0.
Fractional linear mapping // Non-degeneracy condition // Inverse & matrix group duality
Condition: a d - b c ≠ 0 (Determinant Δ ≠ 0)
w = (a/c) (c z + b c/a) / (c z + d) = a/c = CONSTANT
The entire complex plane collapses to a single point! Mapping becomes degenerate.
Conformal everywhere except at the pole z = -d/c (where w = ∞).
Obtained by solving cwz + dw = az + b for z.
[T] = [[a, b], [c, d]] with det([T]) = ad - bc ≠ 0
• Composition of two transformations: [T₂ ∘ T₁] = [T₂] · [T₁] (Matrix product!)
★ Möbius group is isomorphic to Projective General Linear Group PGL(2, C)!
A Bilinear transformation maps circles and straight lines into circles and straight lines!
• A straight line is simply a generalized circle passing through the point at infinity (∞).
Circle passing through pole z = -d/c ⇒ Maps to a STRAIGHT LINE in w-plane.
Circle NOT passing through pole ⇒ Maps to a TRUE CIRCLE in w-plane.
★ Core basis for boundary condition problems in electromagnetic waveguide design!
Proves that EVERY Möbius map is built from translations, rotations, and inversions!
Preservation of projective cross-ratio // Unique construction from 3 point correspondences
The cross-ratio of four distinct points is invariant under any Bilinear map:
If one of the points is ∞, factor it out and take limit → ∞:
The ratio containing that point simplifies to 1!
limᶍ₁→∞ (z - z₁) / (z₂ - z₁) = 1 ⇒ Right side becomes: (z₂ - z₃) / (z - z₃)
limᶍ₂→∞ (z₂ - z₃) / (z₂ - z₁) = 1 ⇒ Right side becomes: (z - z₁) / (z - z₃)
limᶍ₃→∞ (z₂ - z₃) / (z - z₃) = 1 ⇒ Right side becomes: (z - z₁) / (z₂ - z₁)
★ Massive exam time saver: Eliminate terms involving ∞ immediately!
PREPFUSION WORKED DRILL: MAP z = {1, i, -1} → w = {0, 1, ∞}
Left hand side (since w₃ = ∞, omit terms with w₃):
Right hand side with z₁ = 1, z₂ = i, z₃ = -1:
When z = -1 ⇒ denominator is 0 ⇒ w = ∞ (Matches! 100% verified!)
04. FIXED POINTS & HALF-PLANE TO DISK CANONICAL MAPPINGS
Invariant points // Quadratic roots equation // Upper half plane to unit circle map
A point z is called a Fixed Point if it maps to itself: w = f(z) = z.
• A quadratic in z ⇒ has at most 2 fixed points (unless identity map w = z)!
CLASSIFICATION OF MÖBIUS MAPS BY FIXED POINTS:
• 2 Fixed points ⇒ Elliptic, Hyperbolic, or Loxodromic transformation
UPPER HALF-PLANE TO UNIT DISK MAPPING
Standard conformal mapping of Upper Half-Plane Im(z) > 0 into Unit Disk |w| < 1:
where Im(z₀) > 0 and λ ∈ ℝ is a real phase angle.
• Point z = z₀ maps to origin w = 0 (center of disk).
• Real axis Im(z) = 0 maps to boundary circle |w| = 1.
For any real point z = x: |x - z₀| = |x - z̄₀| (symmetric distance!)
Therefore |w| = |eᵢλ| · 1 = 1 ⇒ boundary maps strictly to circle boundary!
GATE EXAM BILINEAR TRAPS & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
Always check determinant before doing calculations.
If ad - bc = 0, mapping is NOT bilinear and NOT conformal anywhere!
GATE question often sneaks this into option D!
In cross-ratio formula, the correspondence z₁→w₁, z₂→w₂, z₃→w₃ must be maintained strictly.
Swapping w₁ and w₂ gives wrong inverted transformation!
Label z₁, z₂, z₃ and w₁, w₂, w₃ explicitly.
Plug in z₁ into each option to see if it gives w₁.
Plug in z₂ to see if it gives w₂.
Solves MCQ in 15 seconds without algebra errors!
